author: Carlos Mathis
title: Air Quality Alert issued for Thursday, June 4 - NewsBreak
text:
By Carlos Mathis Channing King ,
7 hours ago
DAYTON, Ohio (WDTN) — A local organization is alerting the public to concerning air that could impact your health.
An Air Quality Alert has been issued for Thursday, June 4, according to the Miami Valley Regional Planning Commission . It will be in effect for Clark, Darke, Greene, Miami, Montgomery, Preble and Shelby counties.
The Air Quality Index is forecasted at 101. Indexes at that level or higher are considered as “unhealthy for sensitive groups.”
During the day, the formation of ground level ozone is possible.
Potential Air Quality Alert Health Impacts Residents in in the impacted counties should be aware that the air could cause certain health issues.
“Older adults, children, and anyone with respiratory or cardiac diseases should reduce prolonged or heavy exertion,” said MVRPC. “People with asthma should follow their asthma action plans and keep quick-relief medicine handy.”
Although most people in the general public will not be impacted, you are encouraged to take breaks indoors periodically. It is safe for the majority of people to be active outside, MVRPC said.
How can I help during the Air Quality Alert? Drivers can help the environment by carpooling and refueling vehicles at the pump after 8 p.m. If you need to complete yardwork, you are encouraged to cut down on equipment powered by gasoline. Individuals needing to mow their lawn are asked to do so in the evening. For specific questions regarding your health, reach out to your healthcare provider.
